# Every token we send, checked against Lender Price's own published list

**Generated by `docs/longterm/ppe-research/token-registry-check.js`. Run date 2026-08-16.**
Re-run it rather than trusting this page — the vendor can add a value at any time and nothing
tells us when they do.

```
LP_USERNAME=… LP_PASSWORD=… LP_CLIENT_SECRET=… node docs/longterm/ppe-research/token-registry-check.js
LP_… node docs/longterm/ppe-research/token-registry-check.js --snapshot   # refresh the committed copy
```

### The live check is the authority; the offline guard is what makes it stick

The check above needs credentials and a network, so it runs when somebody remembers to run it —
which is no protection at all against an invented token added the next day. So the registry is also
**committed as `vendor-token-registry.json`** (75 fields, with the date it was read), and
`scripts/test-lt-lp-vendor-tokens-pure.js` checks our tables against it **on every `npm test`**, with
no credentials.

The two are not redundant. The offline guard can only ever say *"nothing we emit was invented as of
the day the snapshot was taken"*; it cannot notice the vendor **adding or retiring** a value. Only
the live check can. Refreshing the snapshot is deliberate (`--snapshot`, with a diff to read) and
never automatic — a silently-updated snapshot would rubber-stamp a vendor change nobody looked at.

The guard **refuses to judge rather than pass** when the snapshot is missing, truncated, or has lost
the field a table maps to: reporting "0 unpublished values" out of an empty set is exactly how a
broken check reads like a clean one. Five sabotages were run against it — an invented reserves
token, `4+` put back as a late count, a made-up citizenship, an emptied snapshot, and one field
quietly dropped from the snapshot — and each fails with a named assertion, with a green control on
either side.

---

## Why this had to be built

Every enum table in the LT Lender Price client was reverse-engineered out of the vendor's browser
bundle and out of captured requests. That proved the names **exist**. It never proved they are
spelled the way the pricing API expects, and it could never notice the vendor **adding** a value.

Both failures are silent, and the first one is the dangerous one. Measured live, three separate
times on three different fields, on one scenario (NJ purchase, $500k value / $400k loan, DSCR 1.25,
FICO 760):

> **A token Lender Price does not publish is not refused. It answers HTTP 200 and prices as
> though the field had never been set.**

| field | a real token | a deliberately invented token |
|---|---|---|
| `GLOBAL_RESERVES` | `Reserves_24` → 394 options / 11 programs | `Reserves_5_FAKE` → **371 / 10** |
| `MORT30LATESLAST12M` | `4` → 14 options / 1 program | `9_FAKE` → **394 / 11** |

No error, no warning, no field name — just a different price. That is why these tables are now
checked against the vendor's own list instead of trusted.

## Where the list comes from

`GET /rest/v1/lp-ppe-integration/company/config/{companyId}` with
`Accept: application/json-no-enum` returns ~1.4 MB, inside which
`quickPricer.customConfigs[].pricingConfig.customConfig` is a **stringified** JSON UI model. Its
enum-carrying nodes each have a `path` and a `values` array of `{code, label}`. **75 enum fields**
are published across the three pricer UIs (PriceX, RateX, Home Equity).

Three traps in reading it, each of which produced a confident wrong answer before it was caught —
they are documented in the tool's own header and must not be "simplified" away:

1. **The token is `.code`.** `.label` is what a human sees ("24 Months"); `.value`/`.name` do not
   exist. Reading the wrong key reports the vendor publishing *nothing*, which looks like an empty
   registry rather than a broken reader.
2. **Compare the VALUES of an alias map, never its keys.** `{ "Fixed 5%": "Fixed5" }` means a
   caller may *type* the first and we *send* the second. Comparing keys reported 8 of 9 families as
   mismatched, all of them wrong.
3. **A non-string value is a sentinel, not a token.** `PREPAY_STRUCTURE_NULL` is a `Symbol` meaning
   "explicitly no prepay" and never reaches the wire as text.

## Result — 2026-08-16

**24 token families checked; 1 carries a value the vendor does not publish.** One more could not be
checked at all and is reported as such rather than counted as passing.

| family | ours | vendor | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| reserves · income doc type · prepay structure · borrower type · citizenship | 8 · 25 · 18 · 6 · 7 | same | ✅ exact |
| tradelines · bankruptcy chapter / status / seasoning | 3 · 3 · 3 · 8 | same | ✅ exact |
| foreclosure · short sale · deed in lieu · forbearance | 7 · 7 · 7 · 3 | 8 · 8 · 8 · 4 | ✅ nothing invented (see gaps) |
| late counts · compensation type · property type · attachment type | 5 · 2 · 20 · 3 | same | ✅ exact |
| loan purpose · loan type · mortgage type · lien priority · property use | 3 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 | 7 · 2 · 6 · 2 · 3 | ✅ deliberately narrower — this is a DSCR investment pricer |
| lock days | 13 | 13 | ✅ exact |
| **state** | 56 | 57 | ❌ we can send `MP`, which is not published |
| **charge-off** | 3 | — | ❓ the registry publishes no list for it |

Odd spellings confirmed as genuinely the vendor's, not our typos: `Reserve_6` and `Reserve_none`
singular beside `Reserves_3/9/12/…` plural; `ForeignNationalwithITIN)` with a stray closing
parenthesis; `24Months` unspaced in one pricer and `24 Months` in another.

## What this run found, and what was done about it

### 1. FIXED — the worst mortgage history was pricing as the best (§37.15)

`LATE_COUNT` ended in `'4+'` and the caller's string was sent verbatim as
`MORT{30|60|90|120}LATESLAST{12M|24M}`. The vendor publishes `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4` — there is no
`4+`. Measured, reproducibly, twice:

| sent | options | programs |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | 394 | 11 |
| `1` | 206 | 5 |
| `2` | 0 | 0 |
| `3` | 14 | 1 |
| `4` | 14 | 1 |
| **`4+` (ours)** | **394** | **11** |
| `9_FAKE` | 394 | 11 |

The field discriminates hard, and an unrecognised value is treated as **no lates at all**. A
borrower with four or more 30-day mortgage lates in the last twelve months was being quoted
**11 programs instead of 1** — the single worst credit input this table can express pricing as the
single best.

`LATE_COUNT` is now an alias map: `4+` is still accepted (it is the natural way to say "four or
more" and callers use it) and `4` is what ships. A count the vendor has no token for is refused
here, because upstream will not refuse it. Pinned by `scripts/test-lt-lp-late-count-token-pure.js`
(7 assertions proven to fail on the pre-fix code).

### 2. FIXED — 9 and 36 months of reserves could not be asked for (§37.14)

`RESERVES_TOKENS` carried six of the eight published values, so a caller simply could not state a
9- or 36-month reserve requirement. Both were added after being measured live: they price
identically to `Reserves_12`/`Reserves_24` (394 options / 11 programs) on the plateau where the
field saturates, while the invented control landed off it at 371 / 10.

Note the two pricer UIs disagree — RateX publishes 9 and 36, PriceX does not — and `searchRaw`
carries no pricer id, so "published somewhere" was not enough on its own. The live measurement is
what settled it.

### 3. OPEN — we can send state `MP`, which the vendor does not publish

The vendor publishes 57 state codes including the **obsolete** `CM` (Northern Mariana Islands) and
`TT` (Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands). We carry the modern `MP` and neither of theirs.

**Deliberately not "fixed", because fixing it would mean guessing.** `CM` is historically the
Northern Marianas, but assuming `CM ≡ MP` is exactly the kind of inference this whole exercise
exists to stop. The behaviour could not be measured either: `searchRaw` refuses a request whose
county FIPS is null or contradicts the state, and there is no vendor-accepted county for the
territories to test with. **Question for Lender Price:** is `CM` the code for the Northern Mariana
Islands, and do you accept `MP`? Practical impact is near zero — DSCR investment lending in the
Marianas — so this is recorded rather than acted on.

### 4. OPEN — charge-off cannot be checked

We send `MLCO2yr | MLCO4yr | MLCOSet` for a mortgage charge-off. The registry publishes no field at
`GLOBAL_MortgageChargeOff`, or publishes it under a path we have not identified. This is reported
as **unchecked**, never as passing — "we could not verify this" and "this is correct" are different
answers. **Question for Lender Price:** under which field id are mortgage charge-off seasonings
published?

---

## Pass 2 — sweeping a real request, so no field escapes because nobody mapped it

The table above is **hand-maintained**, which is the exact shape that goes stale silently. It checks
the whole *table* of what each family could send — but only for families somebody remembered to add.
Measured: a real request emitted **eight dynamic fields and a dozen criteria paths that table did
not cover at all**, so "24 families, all ok" was a pass over a subset.

So the checker now also **derives** its field list from what `buildSearch` actually produces, across
three scenarios (minimum facts, every optional field the builder accepts, and a cash-out refinance).
The two passes answer different questions and both are needed: the table can see a value no scenario
happened to emit; the sweep can see a **field** nobody mapped.

**Result: 42 emitted fields resolved against the registry, 0 carrying a value it does not publish.**

Two things that had to be right for that number to mean anything:

- **The registry's `path` IS the request path.** A dotted path addresses the nested request object
  (`criteria.loanPurpose`); a bare name is a `dynamicPropertiesMap` key (`GLOBAL_RESERVES`). Not
  assumed — every path is looked up by that exact string, and the 42 that resolve are the proof.
- **Booleans and numbers are swept too, compared as `String(v)`.** The registry publishes
  `criteria.interestOnly` as the strings `"true" | "false"`, but the **real frontend capture sends a
  JSON boolean** there (verified in anchors req-01 and req-07) and we match it. So the registry's
  values describe the UI's option list while the wire **type** is whatever the frontend sends.
  Collecting only strings made that entire class invisible — the one place a type mismatch could
  hide — and made the discovery list falsely claim we never send those fields. **Parity with the
  capture decides the type; the registry decides the value. Where they could disagree, the capture
  wins and this pass must not "fix" it.**

Eleven emitted fields carry a *word* the registry publishes no list for
(`brokerCriteria.sortView`, `businessSourceType`, `criteria.loanType`, the `accessCriteria` flags…).
Every one of them was checked against the captured frontend request and **all 11 match it exactly**
— a gap in what the registry publishes, not a defect in what we send. Thirty-five more are free
numbers, which have no enum by definition. Both are reported as **unchecked**, never as passed.

## The discovery list — 25 fields the vendor publishes that we never send

This is the list that answers a "the field name was never captured" deferral, and one of them lands
squarely on an open item in `LENDER-PRICE-PARITY-STATUS.md` §2:

> **`Lateinlast24months` — `true | false`.** `field-registry.js` records that the 13–24-month parent
> late toggle "was never captured, so it is deliberately NOT wired — only its per-bucket counts
> are." The vendor publishes the field name and both values. Its 12-month sibling is already wired
> with the confirmed ON token `true`.

Others worth a decision rather than a change: `criteria.nonOccCoBorrower` and
`criteria.numberOfBorrower` (both listed in §2 as "company-specific fields, no capture" — the
registry publishes both), `brokerCriteria.qmTypes` (§2 "QM scope"), `GLOBAL_CONDOTYPE` and
`GLOBAL_HOMEEQUITYTYPE` (§2 "HELOC / lien-priority subtypes"), and `GLOBAL_Section184` /
`GLOBAL_NativeAmerican` (§2, where Section 184 is additionally a compound state machine and must
stay atomic-or-rejected).

**None of these were wired tonight, on purpose.** The registry proves a field name and its permitted
values; it does **not** prove that the frontend sends that field, or when. Parity is measured against
the captured request, so wiring a field the frontend omits would diverge from the thing we are trying
to match. Each of these now needs one capture — or one owner decision — rather than more research,
which is a materially better position than "never captured".

The same reasoning applies to several "off tokens" the code notes as uncaptured
(`Global_DSCR_Asset_Depletion` publishes `No | Yes`; `FirstTimeInvestor`, `Global_Living_Rent_Free`
and `Lateinlast12months` all publish `true | false`). The off value is now **known to be valid** —
what is still unknown is whether the frontend sends it or omits the field, and only a capture
settles that.

## Values the vendor offers that we cannot send

These are not defects. Each is either a deliberate scope decision or a gap worth a decision:

| family | vendor offers, we lack | reading |
|---|---|---|
| foreclosure / short sale / deed in lieu | `FC_Null` · `SS_Null` · `DIL_Null` | an explicit "not set" state, distinct from omitting the field — the same distinction `Reserve_none` carries. Worth adding if a caller ever needs to state it positively. |
| forbearance | `ForbearNone` | same shape |
| loan purpose | `StreamLineRefinance` · `Construction` · `ConstructionPerm` · `VAIRRRL` | out of scope for a DSCR investment pricer |
| loan type | `Variable` | ARMs are out of scope today; the pricer forces `Fixed` |
| mortgage type | `FHA` · `VA` · `UsdaRural` · `HELOC` · `HomeEquity` | out of scope; the pricer forces `Conventional` |
| lien priority | `SecondLien` | out of scope; the pricer forces `FirstLien` |
| property use | `PrimaryResidence` · `SecondaryVacation` | out of scope; investment only |
| state | `CM` · `TT` | see finding 3 |

## A separate thing the probing turned up

Two mortgage lates in the last twelve months prices **0 options / 0 programs**, while *three*
lates prices 14 / 1. A worse input returning more programs than a better one is not something we
can explain from the outside, and it is the vendor's own rules rather than anything in our request.
**Question for Lender Price:** is that intentional?
